- Do not implement unrelated Workbench capabilities or refactor adjacent repositories.
- Do not recreate InferWeave identity, scheduling, model-routing, reservation, accounting, or Resource Safety authority.
- Do not reveal OpenCode, host infrastructure, runtime sockets, or provider authentication material to browsers.

## Design constraints

- Preserve all ten invariants in [the v1 spec](https://github.com/InferWeave/inferweave-workbench/blob/main/docs/specs/2026-08-21-workbench-v1.md).
- Consume published/versioned InferWeave contracts; draft or unpinned upstream artifacts remain explicit blockers.
- Keep OpenCode-specific types behind AgentRuntime and durable state outside browser/process memory.
- Prefer the smallest design that meets v1; no unnecessary distributed infrastructure or new dependency without review.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Use Qwen3.8 through InferWeave and OpenCode on meaningful Workbench issues and capture model, quantization, GPU, context, tokens, speed, retries, tools, tests, review score, intervention, and outcome.
- [ ] Success, unauthorized, invalid-input, interrupted, retry/replay, and recovery behavior is explicit and deterministic where applicable.
- [ ] Documentation and sanitized verification evidence are updated with no known invariant violation or unowned failure mode.

## Tests required

- [ ] Execute the named scenarios against real local/integration services without mock-only acceptance.
- [ ] Preserve reproducible, sanitized evidence and prove the test detects an intentional break.

## Dependencies

Dependency references are hard gates: do not remove blocked labels until the required contracts are merged and pinned.

## Documentation impact

Update the governing architecture/security/operations/user/development documentation and ADRs when behavior or a boundary changes. Add Mermaid diagrams for non-trivial state, sequence, trust, or ownership relationships.

## Security considerations

Apply least privilege, tenant isolation, bounded inputs/outputs, redaction, and safe failure behavior appropriate to this boundary.

## Observability considerations

Emit structured, tenant-safe lifecycle/error/audit signals with correlation identifiers and useful latency/retry/capacity metrics. Never record authentication material, prompt content by default, private file contents, or unredacted tool/MCP data.

## AutoSpec implementation notes

- **Files to read first:** `AGENTS.md`, `docs/specs/2026-08-21-workbench-v1.md`, `docs/architecture/overview.md`, `docs/security/threat-model.md`, and all dependency PRs/contracts.
- **Implementation scope:** issue-scoped branch and PR; TDD; real-service acceptance; small reversible commits; no direct main push.
- **Team personality:** security-sensitive persistent product team (architecture, distributed backend, frontend/UX, platform/sandbox, security, reliability/test).
- **Review counter-team:** independent product, operations, security, accessibility, maintainability, and data-integrity reviewers challenge hidden coupling, unsafe defaults, mock-only proof, and recovery ambiguity.
- **Model fit:** `ctx:32k`, `reasoning:deep`. Qwen3.8-through-InferWeave is appropriate only when risk and benchmark evidence permit; security-critical changes require a different independent reviewer/model.
